source_evidence: This protection limits investor exposure to a set percentage of potential loss. This protection offers a set percentage of loss that the insurance company is willing to absorb before deducting value from the indexed annuity.
question: A 10% floor and a 10% buffer both mean the insurance company absorbs the first 10% of an index decline, right?
answer: No. A floor limits your loss to a set percentage. A buffer means the insurer absorbs a set percentage of the loss before any remaining decline is deducted from the annuity. For example, with a 10% floor and a 12% index decline, you would lose 10% of the contract value; with a 10% buffer, you would lose 2%, before contract adjustments such as surrender charges.
